questions.question: When going through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the same part of your lane the whole time.
Stay in the left part of your lane the whole time.
Stay in the right part of your lane the whole time.
Remember that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change all the time. Be ready to change your lane position when needed. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve of the road exactly.

questions.question: What does a rectangular sign show?
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters show traffic rules, like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally recommended, groups should form a single line when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane offer a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each lane offers three paths: the left side, center, and right side.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or use saddlebags. Stacking loads high on the back can raise the center of gravity and affect balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: How can you discourage other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left part of your lane.
Ride in the center part of your lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver tries to move in.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When another driver might try to squeeze into your lane, ride in the center to stop them from doing so.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: They do not need to reach the footrests.

questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the operator. A child in front may have trouble balancing and could get in the way of the controls.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It supplies at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best, and no lane position should always be avoided. Choose a position based on road conditions.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of a good lane position?

options.text: It helps you see and be seen.
It keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots.
It helps you avoid road hazards.
It blocks access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: It blocks access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen, avoid blind spots and road hazards, discourage drivers from sharing your lane, and provide an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Keep a larger distance from the vehicle ahead.
Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This makes it slower to respond. When carrying a passenger, ride slower than normal, slow down sooner than normal, and keep more distance from other vehicles. You should talk to your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. This makes the motorcycle lean in the right direction.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a rider do?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Honk the horn often when riding at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle's headlights when riding at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, increase your distance from other vehicles, use the headlights of cars ahead to see farther, use your high beam headlight when safe, and be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Try to use only the brakes instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do them separately. You can brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: When stopping, what is the best way to brake?

options.text: Grab the front brake lever suddenly.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look straight ahead.
Apply slow, steady pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look straight ahead.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line stop, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. Press the front brake with more force as weight shifts forward. Reduce rear brake pressure as you slow down. Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.
